source: Salesforce Release Note Changes Okt/Nov 2026 via Salesforce Docs MCP; Texte sind eigene Zusammenfassungen

features.title: Organize Flows with Tags
features.summary: You can classify flows with tags by business area, team or purpose and filter the flow list by them.
features.recommendation: You have {automation.activeFlows|active flow|active flows}. Create two or three tag categories (e.g. business area, object, owner team) and tag your flows once. This makes handovers and clean-ups easier.

recommendationVariants.text: With {automation.activeFlows|active flow|active flows}, a way to organize them is a must: define tag categories first (business area, object, owner team), then tag all flows in one joint clean-up session and filter the flow list by tags from now on.

explainer.what: Flows are the automations in Salesforce, e.g. "When an order is closed, send an email". Larger orgs quickly end up with dozens of them. Now you can give them keywords (tags), such as "Sales" or "Invoices".
explainer.benefit: You find related automations faster. New admins or external partners understand more quickly what each one is for.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing breaks. The flow list just stays as cluttered as it is today.

features.title: Flow Test Mode Is Now Generally Available (GA)
features.summary: Debug and test flows in one place; test scenarios can be saved, automated with assertions and show coverage.
features.recommendation: You have {automation.recordTriggeredFlows|record-triggered flow|record-triggered flows} and {automation.scheduledFlows|scheduled flow|scheduled flows}. Enable Flow Test Mode (Setup > Process Automation Settings) and create saved scenarios with assertions for your most important flows. That way, regressions show up when you make changes later.

recommendationVariants.text: You have {automation.recordTriggeredFlows|record-triggered flow|record-triggered flows}, too many to cover all at once. Enable Flow Test Mode (Setup > Process Automation Settings) and start by creating saved scenarios with assertions for your five most business-critical flows.

You have {automation.scheduledFlows|scheduled flow|scheduled flows}. Enable Flow Test Mode (Setup > Process Automation Settings) and save a test scenario for each scheduled flow. That way, you can safely check nightly runs before making changes.

explainer.what: Whenever you change an automation, you should check that it still works correctly afterwards. Salesforce now has a dedicated test mode for this: you set up an example once ("for this record, the result must be X") and can repeat the test at any time.
explainer.benefit: Errors are caught before go-live, not by your users. Changes to important processes become much safer.
explainer.ifNothing: Everything keeps working as before. But you miss out on a free safety net for changes.

features.title: Mock Outputs for Action and Subflow Elements in Flow Tests (GA)
features.summary: In flow tests, actions and subflows can be replaced with predefined outputs. Callouts and subflows then don't actually run.
features.recommendation: Useful for flows with callouts or subflows: you can test fault paths specifically without putting load on external systems.

explainer.what: Some automations talk to other systems, e.g. an accounting system. When testing, you don't want to actually contact those systems. Now you can store a "pretend" answer for the test.
explainer.benefit: Testing becomes possible without creating real data in other systems. You can also deliberately play through error cases ("the system doesn't respond").
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing changes. Such automations simply remain hard to test.

features.title: Fewer Flow Errors Caused by Record Locks
features.summary: Scheduled flows with a runtime API version of 62 or lower automatically retry once after 10 seconds when they hit UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW.
features.recommendation: {automation.scheduledFlowsApiLe62|scheduled flow benefits|scheduled flows benefit} automatically from the new retry. No action needed. If you've had occasional UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW errors so far, watch whether they decrease.

explainer.what: When two processes try to change the same record at the same time, one of them has to wait. Until now, a scheduled automation would sometimes just give up. Now it waits briefly and tries again.
explainer.benefit: Fewer occasional, hard-to-explain errors in overnight or scheduled processes.
explainer.ifNothing: You don't need to do anything; the improvement takes effect automatically.

features.title: Build Flows Through Conversation with Flow Author (Beta)
features.summary: A VS Code extension that generates a deployable flow from a description; activation remains with a human.
features.recommendation: For teams with Agentforce and Data Cloud: try it out in a sandbox, e.g. for simple schedule-triggered or record-triggered flows. The extension is available through your Salesforce account executive.

explainer.what: With "Flow Author", you describe in plain language what an automation should do, and an AI builds a proposal from it. A human reviews it and switches it on.
explainer.benefit: Simple automations get built faster. This especially helps teams with little admin capacity.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. It's an optional tool (still in beta).

features.title: Conditional Visibility with Reactive Formulas
features.summary: Conditional visibility rules in flow screens can now reference formulas that use components on the same screen.
features.recommendation: You have {automation.screenFlows|screen flow|screen flows}. Review screens where you previously built workarounds for conditional visibility (extra screens, hidden fields). These can now be simplified.

recommendationVariants.text: You have {automation.screenFlows|screen flow|screen flows}. Look specifically for screens with workarounds for conditional visibility (extra screens, hidden helper fields) and simplify the most-used ones first.

explainer.what: Screen flows are guided input forms, e.g. a wizard for logging a case. Fields can now show or hide themselves based on calculations on the same page, without a detour through an extra page.
explainer.benefit: Input forms get shorter and more pleasant for users. Admins save themselves complicated workarounds.
explainer.ifNothing: Existing forms keep working. You just don't benefit from the simplification.

features.title: Find a Record in a Collection Without a Loop
features.summary: The new "Collection Filter Criteria" resource returns the first matching record in a collection; according to Salesforce, much faster than loop constructs.
features.recommendation: With {automation.activeFlows|active flow|active flows}: the next time you touch a flow, replace Loop + Decision + Assignment patterns that only look for a single match with the new resource.

recommendationVariants.text: With {automation.activeFlows|active flow|active flows}, a targeted review is worthwhile: look for Loop + Decision + Assignment patterns that only search for a single match, starting with record-triggered flows on heavily used objects. Each rework saves CPU time and makes flows easier to read.

explainer.what: Automations often need to find one specific record in a list of records. Until now, this required a loop made of several building blocks. Now a single building block does the job.
explainer.benefit: Automations run faster, use less processing time (important for Salesforce limits) and are easier to understand.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing breaks. Existing automations just stay slower and more complicated than necessary.

features.title: "Contains" on Multi-Select Picklists Now Works in Flows
features.summary: The Contains operator on multi-select picklists works in Get/Update/Delete Records and in the entry criteria of scheduled flows. Previously it caused a runtime error.
features.recommendation: Bug fix, takes effect automatically. If you built formula workarounds (INCLUDES) for this, you can simplify them when convenient.

explainer.what: Multi-select fields (e.g. "Interests: A; B; C") couldn't be reliably filtered by "contains" in automations; errors occurred. This is now fixed.
explainer.benefit: Filters on such fields finally work as expected.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing; the bug is fixed automatically.

features.title: Debug, Suspend and Resume Flow Approval Processes
features.summary: Approval admins can suspend and resume approval runs and debug them with run details directly in Flow Builder.
features.recommendation: You use {automation.flowApprovals|flow approval process|flow approval processes}. Assign the approval admin role to the people responsible and add debug/suspend/resume to your operations handbook.

explainer.what: Approval processes (e.g. discount approvals) can now be paused, resumed and investigated directly when problems occur.
explainer.benefit: Stuck or faulty approvals can be sorted out faster, without restarting the whole process.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. But troubleshooting stays time-consuming when problems occur.

features.title: Delete Approval Records in Line with GDPR
features.summary: When the parent record is deleted, ongoing approvals are automatically canceled overnight; completed approvals must be deleted manually.
features.recommendation: Extend your GDPR deletion process: after a record is deleted, completed approval records remain and must be deleted separately.

explainer.what: When you delete a record because of a deletion request (GDPR), its completed approvals remain. They have to be deleted separately.
explainer.benefit: You can truly fulfill deletion requests completely.
explainer.ifNothing: Traces of personal data can remain in approval records. In an audit, that would be a data protection risk.

features.title: Specify Org Responsibilities (Beta)
features.summary: New "Org Responsibilities" Setup page for the security contact, primary admin and partner of record; Salesforce uses it for security and account communication.
features.recommendation: In production, maintain at least one security contact and one primary admin; otherwise security notices from Salesforce may go to the wrong person. If you're a partner: register as partner of record.

explainer.what: Salesforce now asks in Setup who is responsible for security and administration at your company and which partner supports you.
explainer.benefit: Important security notices from Salesforce reach the right person.
explainer.ifNothing: Salesforce keeps reminding you in Setup. Security warnings may end up with someone who is no longer responsible.

features.title: Contextual AI Help Directly in Salesforce
features.summary: An AI help agent answers questions in the context of the current page and permissions (English only). Enterprise from September, Unlimited from October 2026.
features.recommendation: Takes effect automatically via the ? icon. Let your users know briefly, especially that it only speaks English.

explainer.what: Salesforce now has an AI assistant behind the question mark icon. It answers how-to questions that match the page you're currently on (currently in English only).
explainer.benefit: Users find answers themselves without asking the admin.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The assistant is simply available.

features.title: Update the Field Service App (Protection Against Stolen Tokens)
features.summary: From app version 264.1, the Field Service app rotates refresh tokens. Devices with an older version will be logged out regularly after 18 January 2027 and lose unsynced data.
features.recommendation: Bring all technician devices to app version 264.1+ by 18 January 2027 at the latest (via MDM or an email to everyone). Otherwise, data loss during offline work is likely.

explainer.what: The app used by field technicians gets better protection against stolen login credentials. For this, every device needs at least app version 264.1 installed.
explainer.benefit: A lost or compromised device becomes useless to attackers more quickly.
explainer.ifNothing: From 18 January 2027, technicians with an old app version will be logged out again and again. Anything they captured offline and haven't synced yet can be lost.

features.title: Bundle Service Appointments Directly in the Scheduling Console
features.summary: Dispatchers can create bundles directly in the Gantt and the list and schedule them as a single unit.
features.recommendation: If you use or want to use appointment bundling: give your dispatchers a short training. Bundling policies must be configured.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with configured bundling policies.

explainer.what: Several small appointments (e.g. three maintenance jobs in the same building) can be combined into one package. This can now be done directly in dispatch planning.
explainer.benefit: Dispatchers plan faster, technicians drive less.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. You just don't benefit from the simplification.

features.title: Search Org Metadata via an MCP Server (Beta)
features.summary: A hosted MCP server that lets coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor) search org metadata semantically, read-only.
features.recommendation: For teams working with AI coding tools: the generated changes get better because the agent knows your real objects, flows and classes.

explainer.what: AI programming tools can use a new interface to look up which fields, objects and automations exist in your org.
explainer.benefit: Developers and partners who work with AI get more fitting suggestions, because the AI knows your real org.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. It's an optional tool (beta).

features.title: Salesforce in Claude Can Create and Update Records (Beta)
features.summary: Through the Claude integration, you can create and update accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities, tasks and custom objects.
features.recommendation: If you use Claude Enterprise: set write permissions to "Needs Approval" so that every change has to be confirmed.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if Claude Enterprise is connected to Salesforce. This can't be detected from the org.

explainer.what: If you've connected Claude (Anthropic's AI assistant) to Salesforce, you can now also have it create and update records via chat.
explainer.benefit: Faster data entry, e.g. "Create a task after the meeting".
explainer.ifNothing: If you use it and don't set write permissions to "with approval", the AI can change data without asking.

features.title: Aura Responses Without Non-Public Fields (Release Update)
features.summary: Aura action responses no longer contain internal, undocumented system fields. Components that use such fields can break. Mandatory from Spring '27.
features.recommendation: You have {dev.auraBundles|custom Aura component|custom Aura components}. Enable the Release Update in a sandbox and briefly test the components before it's enforced with Spring '27.

recommendationVariants.text: You have {dev.auraBundles|custom Aura component|custom Aura components}. Enable the Release Update in a sandbox first and plan a regression test of all components; with this many, a test checklist pays off. Mandatory from Spring '27.

explainer.what: Older custom-built interface building blocks (Aura) will no longer receive internal, undocumented fields from Salesforce. Anyone who relied on them needs to make fixes.
explainer.benefit: More security, because less internal data is sent to the browser.
explainer.ifNothing: From Spring '27, the change is enforced. Affected building blocks may then show empty values or errors.

features.title: Replace Instanced URLs in API Traffic (Release Update)
features.summary: API calls via incorrect instance URLs no longer work; integrations must use the My Domain URL. SOAP login() via custom domains fails. Sandboxes from October 2026, production from January 2027.
features.recommendation: Check all integrations ({security.connectedApps|connected app|connected apps}): the target URL must be the My Domain URL, and SOAP logins should be switched to OAuth. The rule is already enforced in sandboxes, so test there first.

recommendationVariants.text: Heads-up: your own Apex code still contains old instance URLs (e.g. na12.salesforce.com). Replace them with your My Domain URL or Named Credentials, and also check your integrations ({security.connectedApps|connected app|connected apps}). The rule is already enforced in sandboxes.

explainer.what: Interfaces to other systems must contact Salesforce through your own address ("My Domain") and no longer through old server addresses.
explainer.benefit: More stable connections that survive server moves at Salesforce.
explainer.ifNothing: From January 2027 (in sandboxes already now), interfaces using old addresses will break. Data will then stop flowing between the systems.

features.title: AI Tags in LWC/Aura Are No Longer Supported
features.summary: New or changed components with <ai> or <design:ai> tags can no longer be deployed; existing ones keep running.
features.recommendation: Only relevant if your components use these tags. If you get a deployment error, keep this change in mind.

explainer.what: A specific technical marker ("AI tag") in custom-built components is no longer supported.
explainer.benefit: None; this is a clean-up by Salesforce.
explainer.ifNothing: Existing components keep running. Only the next time you change an affected component will the deployment fail, until the marker is removed.

features.title: Allow External Domains for Visualforce iFrames in the Mobile App
features.summary: In the Salesforce mobile app, external domains can only embed Visualforce pages if they've been allowed.
features.recommendation: You have {dev.vfPages|Visualforce page|Visualforce pages}. If external pages embed them in the mobile app: add the domains under Setup > Session Settings > Trusted Domains for Inline Frames.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if VF pages are embedded by external pages in the mobile app.

explainer.what: When external websites embed Salesforce pages (Visualforce) in the mobile app, those websites now have to be explicitly allowed.
explainer.benefit: Protection against third-party sites embedding your Salesforce content without you noticing.
explainer.ifNothing: Embeds that haven't been allowed are blocked in the app. Affected users will then see a blank area.

features.title: Custom Sharing Reasons on Standard Objects
features.summary: Apex managed sharing on standard objects (e.g. AccountShare) can use custom sharing reasons; such shares survive owner changes.
features.recommendation: If you set shares via Apex with RowCause "Manual": switch to custom sharing reasons. They're no longer lost when the owner changes.

explainer.what: When code shares records with specific people, it can now specify its own "reason". Such shares remain in place when the record's owner changes.
explainer.benefit: Shares are no longer lost when owners change, which saves support cases.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. But shares can still disappear when owners change.

features.title: Rebuild Your Branded Mobile App (Refresh Token Rotation)
features.summary: Since 21 October 2026, Salesforce has been enabling refresh token rotation. Branded apps without support log users out and block them from logging in again.
features.recommendation: If you have your own branded app (Mobile Publisher): rebuild and republish it immediately.
features.checkHint: Whether a branded app exists can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: If you have your own branded Salesforce app (with your own logo in the app store), you need to rebuild it so it supports the new protection against stolen login credentials.
explainer.benefit: More security for mobile access.
explainer.ifNothing: Users of the old app will be logged out and won't be able to log in again.

features.title: Salesforce to Salesforce Is Being Retired (Release Update)
features.summary: From Spring '27, Salesforce to Salesforce no longer works in any org. Alternatives: Partner Cloud, Data Cloud One, MuleSoft.
features.recommendation: You have {integration.s2sConnections|active S2S connection|active S2S connections}. Plan the migration now; after Spring '27, the data exchange stops.

explainer.what: "Salesforce to Salesforce" is an old feature that lets two companies exchange records between their Salesforce orgs. It's being switched off completely.
explainer.benefit: Moving to a modern solution gives you more control and security when exchanging data.
explainer.ifNothing: From Spring '27, the exchange stops. Partner data will then no longer arrive.

features.title: Keep Your Email Verification Exception (Release Update)
features.summary: Exceptions from email address verification set up by Support end on 1 December 2026. Unverified users will then no longer be able to send emails.
features.recommendation: Check whether this Release Update appears in your org. If it does: configure your authorized email domains before 1 December 2026; otherwise users may no longer be able to send emails.
features.checkHint: Setup > Release Updates: only appears in affected orgs.

explainer.what: Some orgs received an exception from Support so that users can send emails without confirming their address. This exception is expiring.
explainer.benefit: More protection against spoofed senders.
explainer.ifNothing: From 1 December 2026, users without a confirmed address can no longer send emails from Salesforce.

features.title: MFA Required for All Employee Logins: Deadline Extension Is Ending (Release Update)
features.summary: For orgs with an MFA deadline extension: once it expires, all internal users must use MFA, including with SSO. The "Waive MFA" exemption permission goes away.
features.recommendation: Check the enforcement date in Setup > Release Updates and make sure all active users have registered an MFA method (Passkey recommended); otherwise they risk being locked out. Tip: with the "Manage Multi-Factor Authentication in API" permission, Release Radar shows the number directly.
features.checkHint: Only applies to orgs with an MFA deadline extension: check Setup > Release Updates.

recommendationVariants.text: Check the enforcement date in Setup > Release Updates. {security.usersWithoutMfaMethod|active user doesn't|active users don't} have an MFA method yet. Have them register one beforehand (Passkey recommended); otherwise they risk being locked out.
Check the enforcement date in Setup > Release Updates. Good news: all active users already have an MFA method. Still, let them know briefly what changes for SSO logins.

explainer.what: MFA means that when you log in, you need a second proof in addition to your password, e.g. an app or a passkey. For orgs that had a postponement, this grace period is now ending.
explainer.benefit: Stolen passwords alone are no longer enough for attackers.
explainer.ifNothing: After the deadline, users without a second method set up can't easily get into Salesforce. Expect lots of support requests on day one.

features.title: Phishing-Resistant MFA for Privileged Users (Release Update)
features.summary: For orgs with a deadline extension: privileged users (System Administrator, Modify/View All Data, Customize Application, Author Apex) must use passkeys/security keys or a corresponding SSO signal.
features.recommendation: You have {security.privilegedUsers|privileged user|privileged users}. Set up passkeys or security keys for them, or configure your IdP to report phishing-resistant MFA.
features.checkHint: Only applies to orgs with a deadline extension: check Setup > Release Updates.

recommendationVariants.text: You have {security.privilegedUsers|privileged user|privileged users}. First check who really needs these permissions and reduce them. For the rest, set up passkeys or security keys, or have your IdP report phishing-resistant MFA.

explainer.what: For admins and other users with far-reaching permissions, a normal second factor will soon no longer be enough. They need an especially secure one, e.g. a passkey or a security key.
explainer.benefit: The most powerful accounts in particular are protected against phishing.
explainer.ifNothing: After the deadline, affected admins without a suitable method won't be able to log in.

features.title: Step-Up Authentication for Report Exports (Release Update)
features.summary: For orgs with a deadline extension: exporting or printing reports requires an additional MFA confirmation, including for SSO users.
features.recommendation: Identify users who export reports and make sure they have an MFA method or a valid email/mobile number. Scheduled reports and the API aren't affected.
features.checkHint: Only applies to orgs with a deadline extension: check Setup > Release Updates.

explainer.what: Anyone who exports or prints a report will have to quickly confirm their identity again (second factor).
explainer.benefit: Makes it harder for large amounts of data to be taken out unnoticed.
explainer.ifNothing: After the deadline, users will be caught by surprise when exporting. Without a registered method or a valid phone number/email, they can't continue.

features.title: Refresh Tokens Expire After 30 Days of Inactivity
features.summary: A 30-day idle limit applies to all connected apps and external client apps. Inactive tokens expire immediately on enforcement; in production since 4 November 2026.
features.recommendation: You have {security.connectedApps|connected app|connected apps}. Check integrations that run rarely (e.g. monthly or quarterly jobs): they must be reauthorized after 30 days of inactivity. Build in error handling for expired tokens.

recommendationVariants.text: You have {security.connectedApps|connected app|connected apps}. Make a list of all integrations and how often they run. Anything that runs less often than every 30 days (monthly, quarterly, yearly jobs) needs error handling for expired tokens or a regular call.

explainer.what: Interfaces log in to Salesforce with a long-lived key. If this key isn't used for 30 days, it now expires automatically.
explainer.benefit: Forgotten, unused access can no longer be misused.
explainer.ifNothing: Rarely running interfaces (e.g. quarterly syncs) fail on their next run and have to be reconnected. This has applied in production since 4 November 2026.

features.title: Step-Up Authentication for Sensitive Setup Settings
features.summary: Optional: a repeat MFA confirmation for sensitive Setup changes (password policies, SSO, connected apps, user data).
features.recommendation: Recommended for all orgs: enable it under Setup > Identity Verification. It prevents someone from changing settings through a hijacked admin session.

explainer.what: For particularly sensitive changes in Setup (e.g. password rules, single sign-on), you can require a repeat confirmation with a second factor.
explainer.benefit: Even if someone hijacks an open admin session, they can't change the most important settings.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing changes. You just miss out on an extra layer of protection.

features.title: New Authentication Signals in Security Health Check
features.summary: New high-risk signal "MFA for all direct UI logins" and three passkey signals; your Health Check score may change as a result.
features.recommendation: Open Health Check, assess the new signals and manually update your own baselines.
features.checkHint: The new signals require the Security Center add-on.

explainer.what: The security health check in Setup now rates additional points around logging in. Your score may change as a result.
explainer.benefit: You see more quickly where there are gaps in login security.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. But your security score may drop without you knowing why.

features.title: Delete Conversation Data Directly from Flow or Apex
features.summary: Messaging end users and conversations can now be deleted via a flow action or Apex, without a custom REST integration.
features.recommendation: Ideal for GDPR deletion requests: integrate the deletion of messaging data into your existing deletion flow (enable the Conversation Data API in Setup).

explainer.what: Chat histories with customers (e.g. WhatsApp, web chat) can now be deleted directly through automation, without custom programming.
explainer.benefit: GDPR deletion requests can be fulfilled completely and automatically.
explainer.ifNothing: You'll still have to delete chat data the hard way, or not at all. That's a data protection risk.

features.title: Reply Suggestions for Multiple Requests in One Message
features.summary: Service Replies recognize multiple requests in a single customer message and suggest a separate reply for each one.
features.recommendation: If you use Service Replies: enable Multi-Intent Detection (Setup > Einstein Reply Recommendations). It may first need to be activated by Salesforce.

explainer.what: When a customer asks several questions in one message, the AI now suggests a separate answer for each question.
explainer.benefit: Service agents reply faster and don't forget any part of the question.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The AI keeps suggesting just one answer.

features.title: Withdrawn: Multi-Intent Article Recommendations
features.summary: The announced multi-intent article recommendations have been postponed to a later release.
features.recommendation: If you had planned for this feature: take it out of your plans.

explainer.what: An announced AI feature (article suggestions for multiple requests) has been postponed by Salesforce.
explainer.benefit: None; the feature isn't coming for now.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Just don't plan around this feature.

features.title: Trade Promotion: Understand How P&L Values Are Derived
features.summary: The new "Calculation Insights" tool shows how a promotion's P&L figures are calculated, including formulas and dependencies.
features.recommendation: If you use Trade Promotion Management: enable "Enable_Calculation_Insights" in Setup > Custom Settings and give your key account managers a short briefing.

explainer.what: For sales promotions with retailers, Salesforce calculates profit and costs automatically. Until now, it was hard to tell how a number came about. Now the calculation steps can be displayed.
explainer.benefit: Users clear up unexpected numbers themselves instead of opening a ticket.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. When questions about numbers come up, it stays a guessing game.

features.title: Trade Promotion: Search Picklists in the Promotion Wizard
features.summary: Long picklists in the promotion wizard (e.g. template, customer, brand) can now be searched by typing.
features.recommendation: For long lists (customers, brands), turn on search per list in the promotion wizard configuration. It's off by default.

explainer.what: When creating a sales promotion, you pick from lists that can be very long. Now you can simply type a few letters instead of scrolling.
explainer.benefit: Faster data entry and fewer wrongly selected values.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The lists stay tedious to use.

features.title: Course Versions Carry Over Admission Requirements
features.summary: When a course version is copied, its stored requirements (e.g. prior knowledge) are now copied automatically as well.
features.recommendation: Takes effect automatically. Take a look at course versions you created recently: requirements may still be missing there.

explainer.what: When a university created a new version of a course, the participation requirements used to get lost. Now they're carried over.
explainer.benefit: No more silent data gaps in course planning.
explainer.ifNothing: You don't need to do anything. But older versions that were already copied stay incomplete until you fill them in.

features.title: Agentforce: A Customer's Open Cases at a Glance
features.summary: The new Agentforce action "Get Recent Open Cases" returns a customer's five most recent open cases with status and priority.
features.recommendation: If you have the "Agentforce for Energy & Utilities" add-on: add the action to your employee agent. Keep an eye on Flex Credits consumption.

explainer.what: The AI assistant for employees can now summarize a customer's open issues on request.
explainer.benefit: Employees immediately see what's open for the customer, without a lengthy search.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The action just isn't available to you.

features.title: Faster Setup of Tariff Comparison and Multisite quoting
features.summary: Salesforce Go now offers solution bundles that bring the setup of Tariff Comparison and Multisite quoting together in one place.
features.recommendation: If you want to introduce Tariff Comparison or Multisite quoting: set them up via Salesforce Go > Energy and Utilities Sales Accelerator instead of by hand.

explainer.what: Instead of hunting down lots of settings one by one, there's now a guided setup path.
explainer.benefit: Less effort and fewer mistakes during rollout.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Setup stays manual and more time-consuming.

features.title: Keep Flexible Hierarchies Up to Date Automatically
features.summary: Two included flows detect outdated rule-based hierarchies (e.g. households, company groups) and update only the affected parts.
features.recommendation: Clone, schedule and activate the two flows "Check Flexible Hierarchy Sync Status" and "Re-Run Out-of-Sync Flexible Hierarchies".

explainer.what: Banks and insurers map out relationships, such as households or company groups. These structures go out of date when data changes. Now there's an automatic update.
explainer.benefit: Relationship structures stay correct without anyone checking them by hand.
explainer.ifNothing: Hierarchies can go out of date unnoticed and lead to wrong reports.

features.title: Route Referrals More Intelligently
features.summary: Customer referrals get new assignment logic, conditional confirmation pages and automatic pre-filling of the referring person.
features.recommendation: Review your assignment rules and enable "Auto-Populate Referrer Details" (off by default).

explainer.what: When an advisor refers a customer to a specialist, the referral now reaches the right person more precisely. The form partly fills itself in.
explainer.benefit: Referrals are handled faster, with fewer typos.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Referrals keep working as before.

features.title: AI Summaries in Healthcare Get Faster and Cheaper
features.summary: The included templates for AI summaries (patient, member, provider) use less AI capacity and load faster.
features.recommendation: Takes effect automatically. If you've customized the templates, compare your changes with the new structure.

explainer.what: Salesforce summarizes patient information using AI. The templates for this have been slimmed down.
explainer.benefit: Shorter wait times and lower consumption of AI credits.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing, except for templates you've customized yourself: they only benefit after you align them.

features.title: Plan Home Visits with Calendar and List Views
features.summary: Home visit planning gets calendar views (day to year), status colors, filters and drag-and-drop rescheduling.
features.recommendation: Add the "Home Health Visits" component to the person or resource page in Lightning App Builder and configure its fields.

explainer.what: Home care services now plan their home visits in a proper calendar, and appointments are easy to move.
explainer.benefit: Faster planning and a better overview for dispatchers.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Planning stays with the old view.

features.title: AI Agent Takes Claim Reports
features.summary: A new agent takes first notices of loss by phone or portal, verifies identity, creates the claim and offers a callback.
features.recommendation: With Agentforce for Financial Services: set up the agent in a sandbox and test it with typical claim cases before it goes live.

explainer.what: Policyholders can report a claim around the clock. An AI agent asks for everything needed and creates the case.
explainer.benefit: Routine reports are handled without a claims handler, so the team can focus on complex cases.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Claim reports keep going through your staff.

features.title: Find Accounts on the iPad by Relevance
features.summary: Account search in the Life Sciences iPad app now sorts results by relevance instead of alphabetically and shows which field matched.
features.recommendation: Takes effect automatically. Briefly let your field team know about the new sorting and the filters.

explainer.what: Pharma field reps search for doctors and practices on the iPad. The best matches are now at the top.
explainer.benefit: Faster finding, even offline.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The improvement takes effect automatically.

features.title: Custom Life Sciences Apps Usable Offline Right Away
features.summary: The mobile app downloads custom app components with every sync, so they also run offline without a previous online session.
features.recommendation: Takes effect automatically. Test your offline-capable custom apps once on a freshly set-up device.

explainer.what: Custom-built extensions of the field app now work offline, even if the device has never used them online before.
explainer.benefit: The field team can start working immediately, even in dead zones.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The improvement takes effect automatically.

features.title: Build and Maintain Household Names Automatically
features.summary: Household names (e.g. "The Miller Family") are built automatically from a template and adjusted immediately when members change.
features.recommendation: With the "Automatic Household Creation and Naming" add-on: enable Setup > Household Naming Settings and create a naming template.

explainer.what: Fundraising organizations group people into households. Until now, their names didn't update themselves. Now they adjust automatically when someone moves in or out.
explainer.benefit: Correct salutations in donor letters without manual work.
explainer.ifNothing: Household names keep going out of date and have to be corrected by hand.

features.title: Set Up Volunteer Management with an AI Agent (Beta)
features.summary: AI agents can turn on Volunteer Management, assign permissions and create the program including its records, e.g. via Agentforce Vibes or Claude Code.
features.recommendation: For new volunteer programs: try the agent-based setup in a sandbox; it saves a lot of clicking.

explainer.what: Instead of clicking everything together in Setup, you describe to an AI agent what the volunteer program should look like, and it sets it up.
explainer.benefit: Faster setup, even without deep Salesforce knowledge.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Setup stays manual.

features.title: Answer Citizens' Tax Questions Automatically
features.summary: The new "Tax Advocate" agent answers questions about refunds, account balances and filing status in the citizen portal, based on Taxpayer 360 data.
features.recommendation: With Public Sector Solutions, Agentforce, Data 360 and Experience Cloud: create the agent from the template, add it to the portal and test it with real questions.

explainer.what: Citizens often ask the same things, e.g. "Where's my refund?". An AI agent answers this in the portal using the existing data.
explainer.benefit: Fewer routine requests for your staff.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Requests keep going through your staff.

features.title: Targeted Recruiting Campaigns from the Applicant Pool
features.summary: Recruiters can filter the applicant pool by skills and previous applications and contact suitable candidates directly (with consent).
features.recommendation: With Talent Recruitment Management and Marketing Cloud: start the setup via Salesforce Go. Known issue: the "Deploy Data Streams" step can hang.

explainer.what: Instead of only waiting for new applications, you can reach out again to previous applicants with matching skills.
explainer.benefit: Positions get filled faster.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Your existing applicant pool stays unused.

features.title: Stage Management: Run Steps Only Under Certain Conditions
features.summary: In Stage Management, you can set a condition directly on a step. If it isn't met, the step is skipped.
features.recommendation: Review existing stage definitions for workarounds (e.g. helper steps for conditions) and switch them to inline conditions.

explainer.what: Multi-stage processes (e.g. application processes) can now simply skip steps when they aren't needed.
explainer.benefit: Simpler, clearer process definitions.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Processes stay more complicated than necessary.
